Shift dates to a new time period

Source: R/anon_fns.R
anon_date_shift.Rd

Shifts dates to a new time period while preserving relative relationships between dates. Supports Date and POSIXct vectors and ISO 8601 character strings such as SDTM --DTC variables.

Usage

anon_date_shift(
  x,
  center_date = Sys.Date(),
  scramble = FALSE,
  offset = NULL,
  partial = c("shift", "remove")
)

Arguments

x

A Date, POSIXct or ISO 8601 character vector to anonymize

center_date

New center point for the date range (default: current date). Ignored when offset is given.

scramble

Logical, whether to randomize the assignment order of generated results. Not available with offset or character input.

offset

Optional number of days (a whole number, or a difftime) to add to every value. Use the same offset for all columns that must stay aligned.

partial

How to handle partial ISO 8601 dates in character input: "shift" (default) moves the middle of the month or year by the offset and keeps the original precision; "remove" replaces them with "".

Value

A vector of the same class as x (character for character input).

Details

By default, dates are moved so that their mean falls on center_date. Each call computes its own shift, so separate columns or datasets move by different amounts. To keep intervals between columns and datasets (for example dose and sample times), pass the same offset to every call.

Character input is read as ISO 8601 and returned as character in the same format and precision: a full date (2014-01-02) is shifted and any time part (after T, t or a space) is kept as is. Partial dates (2014-03, 2014, and the SDTM forms 2014-03--T08:00 and 2014---15) are handled by partial. Both date ends of an interval (2014-01-02/2014-01-05) are shifted; a duration end (2014-01-02/P1D) is kept. Time-only values (-----T07:15), durations, empty strings and NA are returned unchanged. Other values, including a month and day without a year (--12-15), and values whose shifted year would fall outside 0001-9999, are removed with a warning.

Examples

dates <- as.Date(c("2023-01-15", "2023-02-20", "2023-03-10"))
anon_date_shift(dates, center_date = "2024-06-01")
#> [1] "2024-05-02" "2024-06-07" "2024-06-25"

# One offset for every column keeps intervals between them
offset <- -400
anon_date_shift(c("2023-01-15T08:00", "2023-02-20", "2023-03"), offset = offset)
#> [1] "2021-12-11T08:00" "2022-01-16"       "2022-02"         
anon_date_shift(as.Date("2023-01-16"), offset = offset)
#> [1] "2021-12-12"
